title: Trump Slams LeBron as “Total Disgrace” Over Anthem Antics in 76ers Debut – Fox News
body:
President Donald Trump reignited his feud with NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday, denouncing the basketball icon’s conduct during the national anthem at James’s first game wearing Philadelphia 76ers apparel. In a post on his Truth Social platform, the former president called James a “total disgrace,” condemning the player’s decision to practice golf swings while the anthem played. The remarks, which quickly spread across social media, have added another chapter to a long‑standing cultural clash between Trump and the league’s most high‑profile figure.

James, who was officially introduced as a member of the 76ers on Monday, entered the arena in a custom‑designed jersey and cap emblazoned with the team’s colors. As the United States flag rose and “The Star‑Spangled Banner” began, cameras captured James standing near the bench, repeatedly swinging an imaginary golf club. The gesture, which he later explained as a light‑hearted nod to his love of the sport and a way to “keep the energy up,” was met with a mixture of amusement and criticism from fans and commentators alike. While some praised the star for injecting personality into a solemn moment, others argued that the anthem deserved reverence, especially given the heightened political sensitivities surrounding sports protests in recent years.

Trump’s tirade on Truth Social was swift and pointed. He wrote, “LeBron James is a total disgrace. Practicing golf swings during the anthem shows a lack of respect for our flag, our troops, and the country. This is the kind of behavior that erodes American values.” The post was accompanied by a still image of James mid‑swing, underscoring the former president’s focus on the visual spectacle. Within minutes, the tweet‑style message garnered thousands of likes, shares, and a flood of replies from both supporters and detractors. Critics of Trump noted that his condemnation mirrors previous attacks on athletes who have knelt or taken a knee during the anthem, framing the issue as a broader cultural war over patriotism and free expression.

The exchange revives a rivalry that has spanned more than a decade. Trump has repeatedly singled out James for perceived political activism, from the 2016 campaign’s “Make America Great Again” rallies to the 2020 election, where the former president accused the star of “pandering to the left.” James, for his part, has largely stayed out of direct political confrontation, preferring to focus on community initiatives and his burgeoning media empire. However, his recent comments about the anthem incident—emphasizing that the gesture was meant “in good fun” and not as a political statement—have drawn renewed scrutiny. Sports analysts suggest that the timing is significant: James’s debut with the Sixers comes at a moment when the NBA is navigating its own internal debates over player activism, league branding, and fan expectations.

The incident also highlights the evolving role of athletes as cultural symbols. In the past, gestures during the anthem have been interpreted as protest; now, even seemingly benign actions like a golf swing can ignite political backlash. Media scholars point out that the convergence of social media, celebrity culture, and partisan polarization creates an environment where any deviation from a perceived norm can be weaponized. For the NBA, the episode serves as a reminder of the delicate balance between allowing personal expression and maintaining a unified presentation of national symbols, especially as the league expands its global footprint and seeks to attract a broader audience.

Looking ahead, the fallout may influence both James’s integration into Philadelphia and the broader discourse on patriotism in sports. The Sixers organization has yet to issue an official statement, but insiders suggest they will stand by the player, emphasizing his commitment to the community and the team’s focus on on‑court performance. Meanwhile, Trump’s criticism is likely to echo through upcoming political rallies, where the former president often leverages high‑profile cultural moments to rally his base. As the NBA season progresses, the league may find itself navigating renewed scrutiny over player conduct during the anthem, a debate that could shape policies and public perception for years to come.
